units.title: The physically literate individual demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns

outcomes.text: Executes basic locomotor skills (i.e. walk, run, hop, skip, jump, gallop, slide, leap).
Performs hopping, skipping, galloping, sliding and leaping competently.
Achieves mature form* of running.
Utilizes correct mechanics* for take-off and landing while jumping for height and for distance.
Demonstrates body awareness and control by performing a variety of shapes (e.g. wide, narrow, curled, twisted, and stretched, etc.).
Sustains a stationary pose on various bases of support.
Controls body while balancing in a variety of shapes on different levels and bases of support.
Transfers weight appropriately between bases of support.
Throws underhand while stepping forward with opposite foot.
Catches a large ball before it bounces twice.
Dribbles a ball at least two times with one hand.
Dribbles a ball forward with the inside of the dominant foot.
Kicks a ball with the top of the foot.
Volleys upward a large, slow-moving object.
Strikes a slow-moving object using a short implement.
Jumps a self-turned rope at least once.

Performs the following skills with 2-3 critical elements* of a mature pattern: throwing (overhand and underhand), catching, dribbling with hands, kicking, volleying (underhand and overhead), striking (short and long implements).
Dribbles with either foot and maintains control of the ball for a short distance.
Strikes a slow-moving object upward repeatedly using a short implement.
Strikes a stationary object with a long implement.
Jumps a self-turned rope repeatedly and a long rope at least five times.
Developmentally appropriate outcomes first appear in Grade 6.
Performs rhythmic activities created by the teacher and/or students.
Developmentally appropriate outcomes first appear in Grade 6.

units.title: The physically literate individual applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance

subtopics.title: Movement concepts, principles and knowledge (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Names various locomotor movements performed in general space and personal space.
Recognizes different body parts and their relation to movement.
Explains three different movement pathways (e.g. straight, curved, zigzag, etc.).
Regulates movement in general space by speed.

subtopics.title: Movement concepts, principles and knowledge (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Demonstrates multiple levels of movement, speed, direction, rhythm, pathways, force, time.
Applies corrective feedback to movement errors during performance.
States the short-term effects of physical activity on the heart and lungs.

units.title: The physically literate individual demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness

outcomes.text: States the benefits of being physically active.
Recognizes the relationship between movement, heart rate and breathing (i.e. increased movement causes increased heart rate and faster breathing).
Names physical activities that enhance fitness.
Developmentally appropriate outcomes first appear in Grade 3.
Distinguishes between healthy and unhealthy foods.
Describes the relationship between food, energy, and physical activity.

units.title: The physically literate individual exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others

outcomes.text: Plays independently with responsible personal behavior.
Accepts corrective feedback from the teacher.
Works cooperatively with the teacher and others.
Follows instructions and class procedures.
Follows the teacher’s instructions regarding safety procedures.

units.title: The physically literate individual recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction

outcomes.text: Identifies physical activities that enhance health.
Recognizes physical activities that are challenging.
Identifies physical activities that provide opportunities for self-expression and enjoyment.

units.title: The physically literate individual demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns

outcomes.text: Selects sprinting or jogging as appropriate for short- and long-distance running.
Links a variety of locomotor skills into a continuous movement sequence.
Balances and/or transfers weight on apparatus or with a partner.

Performs the following skills with 4-5 critical elements* of a mature pattern: throwing (overhand and underhand), catching, dribbling with hands, kicking, volleying (underhand and overhead), striking (short and long implements).
Throws to a target or partner with objects of varied weight and size while stationary or moving.
Catches a thrown or batted ball while moving or stationary at high, medium, and low levels.
Dribbles with either hand while jogging.
Passes and receives a ball with the feet while moving.
Volleys underhand over a net or to a target.
Strikes a stationary or moving object to a partner or in a game situation, using short and/or long implements.
Jumps with short or long ropes in a self-created jump rope routine.
Developmentally appropriate outcomes first appear in Grade 6.
Creates an original dance utilizing a combination of locomotor skills and movement concepts (e.g. changes in speed, direction, level, flow, etc.).
Performs cultural dances (i.e. folk and square dance) with proper rhythm and movement.

units.title: The physically literate individual applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance

subtopics.title: Movement concepts, principles and knowledge (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Describes how heart rate and other biological indicators are used to monitor exercise intensity.
Explains the importance of practice for improving skill performance.
Recognizes the necessity of transferring weight from the back leg to the front leg during any action that propels an object forward.
Identifies the key elements of a catch and provides feedback to a fellow student.

subtopics.title: Movement concepts, principles and knowledge (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Applies appropriate force while dribbling a ball with hands.
Describes foot placement when dribbling a ball and for kicking a stationary or moving ball.
Identifies the key elements of a proper grip when holding a short or long implement.
Applies movement concepts to strategies used in games (e.g. direction, force, speed, pathways, etc.).
Executes basic offensive and defensive strategies and tactics used in a variety of activities, invasion games, net/wall games, throws, volleys, and striking.

units.title: The physically literate individual demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness

outcomes.text: Recognizes the effects of different levels of exertion during physical activity (i.e. sedentary vs. vigorous).
Lists the components of health-related fitness (cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular endurance, muscular strength, flexibility, body composition).
Recalls the components of skill related fitness (agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time, speed).
Describes the importance of warm-up and cool-down.
Defines the target heart zone.
Explains the importance of exercising in the target heart zone.
Analyzes and interprets results of fitness assessments.
Sets goals for improvement of physical fitness based upon a fitness assessment.
Chooses foods that support participation in sport and physical activity.
Recognizes the importance of hydration during and after physical activity.

units.title: The physically literate individual exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others

outcomes.text: Participates responsibly both independently and with others.
Accepts responsibility if personal behavior affects others negatively.
Uses equipment responsibly and appropriately.
Provides encouragement to peers.
Works with peers of all skill abilities.
Demonstrates socially acceptable conflict resolution strategies.
Adheres to rules and accepts consequences for infractions.
Follows safety procedures without reminders.

units.title: The physically literate individual recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction

outcomes.text: Describes the health benefits of physical activity.
Selects physical activities based on personal levels of challenge.
Expresses positive feelings when participating in physical activities inside or outside of school.
Exhibits positive attitudes towards physical activity while interacting with peers.
Communicates effectively with others to establish positive social interaction during physical activities.

units.title: The physically literate individual demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns

outcomes.text: Combines locomotor skills and manipulative skills (i.e. throwing, catching, dribbling, kicking and striking) in various activities.
If the learner did not attain the outcomes by Grade 5, they should be the focus through Grade 8.
Performs manipulative skills consistently with a mature pattern.
Executes manipulative skills with dominant and nondominant hand or foot.
Demonstrates basic offensive skills (i.e. pivot, fake, jab step, screen) in modified and small-sided games.
Performs defensive skills (i.e. drop step, defensive stance and movement) in modified and small-sided games.
Changes direction and speed as necessary during gameplay.
Designs original movement sequences to music with proper timing.
Executes synchronized original dance movements with another individual or group.
Performs beginner social dances with a partner or group (e.g. ballroom dance, line dance, etc.).
Participates competently in lifetime activities such as individual/dual sports and self-defense.

units.title: The physically literate individual applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance

outcomes.text: Utilizes instructional cues to self-assess while performing complex skills in dance, gymnastics, and invasion games.
Selects practice procedures to learn and master skills and movement patterns.
Evaluates and applies safe protocol to activities based on weather, levels of difficulty, and ability.
Applies appropriate speed, trajectory, direction, pathway, and positioning for game play.
Creates or reduces space in invasion games through approach or retreat.
Selects an offensive or defensive tactic while performing with or without objects.
Calibrates the full width and length of the field or court to regulate personal speed and movement during play.
Manages performance angles, force, and direction to gain or deny competitive advantage.
Communicates with teammates effectively during game play.

units.title: The physically literate individual demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness

outcomes.text: Explains how physical activity benefits physical, mental, and social health.
Identifies major muscle groups used in various physical activities.
Lists the components of health-related fitness (cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular endurance, muscular strength, flexibility, body composition).
Recalls the components of skill related fitness (agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time, speed).
Describes the importance of warm-up and cool-down.
Defines the target heart zone.
Explains the importance of exercising in the target heart zone.
Explains the FITT principle (Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type).
Sets SMART (specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and timely) goals to improve or maintain three areas of health-related fitness based on a fitness assessment.
Develops a personal fitness program by applying the FITT principle.
Maintains a physical activity and/or nutrition log reflecting the results of a self-assessment.
Uses MY PLATE to define basic food groups and explain the healthy balance between food, water and physical activity.
Describes the health risks of poor nutrition.
Recognizes situations that produce stress.
Performs stress-reducing activities such as yoga, deep breathing, and progressive muscle relaxation.

units.title: The physically literate individual exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others

outcomes.text: Assumes responsibility for improving their personal fitness.
Respects others by using self-management skills to adjust behavior as necessary.
Utilizes corrective feedback from teacher and peers.
Accepts peers with different ideas, cultural background, and body types in physical activities.
Resolves conflict in a variety of class settings.
Officiates modified physical activities and games utilizing appropriate rules and etiquette.
Follows guidelines for completing group or individual projects (e.g. designing games, creating dance routines, etc.).
Recognizes safety concerns associated with particular activities and makes choices to protect self and others from injury.

units.title: The physically literate individual recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction

outcomes.text: Expresses interest in specific activities based on personal health goals
Demonstrates appropriate response to challenging physical activities (e.g. increased effort, asking for help, modifying the activity, etc.).
Participates in physical activity that allow for self-expression and enjoyment (e.g. dance, gymnastics, etc.).
Supports others’ enjoyment of physical activity by demonstrating respect for differences, fair play, conflict resolution and sportsmanship.
Expresses a desire to interact with others socially through sports and games.
Demonstrates responsible social behavior and appropriate relationships with peers in physical activity settings.

units.title: The physically literate individual demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns

outcomes.text: If the learner did not attain the outcomes by Grade 8, they should be the focus in the required HS program.
If the learner did not attain the outcomes by Grade 8, they should be the focus in the elective HS program.
If the learner did not attain the outcomes by Grade 5, they should be the focus in the required HS program.
If the learner did not attain the outcomes by Grade 5, they should be the focus in the elective HS program.
If the learner did not attain the outcomes by Grade 8, they should be the focus in the required HS program.
If the learner did not attain the outcomes by Grade 8, they should be the focus in the elective HS program.
Selects and uses appropriate offensive and defensive skills in a variety of individual, dual and team activities.
If the learner did not attain the outcome in Level 1, it should be a focus in Level 2.
Performs intermediate or advanced dances appropriate for social settings (i.e. weddings or community gatherings).
Exhibits competency in one or more forms of theatre dance (i.e. ballet, modern, tap, jazz, hip hop, ethnic).
Choreographs and presents an original theatre dance piece (solo or group).
Demonstrates ability in one or more lifetime activities (e.g. individual/dual sports, outdoor sports, swimming, self-defense, etc.).
Exhibits proficiency in two or more lifetime activities.

units.title: The physically literate individual applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance

outcomes.text: Uses performance terminology accurately (e.g. “balance,” “follow through,” “eye on the ball,” etc.) for a variety of activities.
Designs a conditioning program for a self-selected game/activity to engage in for life.
Explains the impact of participation in selected sports and activities on various components of fitness.
Explains the historical and cultural roles that games, sports, and dance play in society.
Analyzes biomechanical principles related to performing motor skills.
Identifies principles used to improve skill performance (force, motion, rotation, speed, accuracy).
Explains accurately the steps for performing basic motor skills.
Transfers tactical knowledge from one sport to a similar sport.
Applies offensive or defensive tactics and strategies to move or block opponent.
Designs a practice plan for improving skills and game play.

units.title: The physically literate individual demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness

outcomes.text: Describes the relationship between physical activity, nutrition and body composition.
Appraises health risk factors associated with a sedentary lifestyle.
Identifies benefits of a physically active lifestyle and its relationship to educational and professional success.
Evaluates barriers that prevent participation in lifetime physical activity and creates solutions to overcome these barriers.
Utilizes technology to monitor heart rate and maintain target heart zone.
Explains principles for performing strength training exercises safely and effectively.
Compares and selects appropriate stretching methods (dynamic or static).
Describes basic training principles (e.g. overload, specificity, progression, diminishing return, rest, and recovery, etc.) and how they improve fitness.
If the learner did not attain the outcome in Level 1, it should be a focus in Level 2.
Sets realistic short-term and long-term goals for all five healthrelated fitness components.
Uses training principles to design a personal workout.
Implements a personal fitness plan that includes assessment scores, goals for improvement, plan for improvement, activity log, and timelines.
If the learner did not attain the outcome in Level 1, it should be a focus in Level 2.
Creates a nutrition plan based on individual caloric needs for one week that includes meals, snacks, and hydration needs.
Compares and contrasts a nutrition plan for an active lifestyle and a sedentary lifestyle.
Selects appropriate stress management methods in response to hypothetical stressful scenarios.
Is proactive in planning management strategies before stressful situations occur.

units.title: The physically literate individual exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others

outcomes.text: Exhibits a positive self-image regarding their physical skills and fitness.
If the learner did not attain the outcome in Level 1, it should be a focus in Level 2
Provides feedback to promote team or group dynamics.
Uses communication skills and strategies to share feedback in a leadership role (e.g. group leader, referee, coach, etc.).
Seeks to include diverse peers in group activities.
Thinks critically and leads group members in implementing conflict resolution strategies.
Displays moral and ethical conduct in specific competitive situations.
Encourages teammates to exhibit proper etiquette and respect for opponents during game play.
Prevents injury to self and others by utilizing appropriate safety measures in preparation for activity (e.g. warmup, proper clothing, hydration, etc.).
If the learner did not attain the outcome in Level 1, it should be a focus in Level 2.

units.title: The physically literate individual recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction

outcomes.text: Selects and participates in physical activities that will enhance a healthy lifestyle.
Explains how physical activity can add value to both physical and emotional health.
Expresses feelings of success and confidence from participation in challenging physical activities.
If the learner did not attain the outcome in Level 1, it should be a focus in Level 2.
Recognizes that enjoyment of certain activities will shift as physical abilities and preferences change over time.
If the learner did not attain the outcome in Level 1, it should be a focus in Level 2.
Selects and participates in physical activities for the purpose of social interaction.
Seeks physical activity opportunities for social interaction outside of school.
